72039-the-story-of-a-woolly-dog.title: Woolly Dog
72039-the-story-of-a-woolly-dog.creator: Laura Lee Hope
72039-the-story-of-a-woolly-dog.description: A book by Laura Lee Hope. “The Woolly Dog is the best toy of all,” went on Mrs. Clark, who kept the little store. “The agent said I could sell him for a good sum and make money on him. Certainly he is a fine toy and I did not have to pay very much, and, since I gave him a bath and cleaned him, he looks good enough to be in a rich store.

arxiv-2003-11013.title: Tractogram filtering of anatomically non-plausible fibers with geometric deep learning
arxiv-2003-11013.creator: Pietro Astolfi, Ruben Verhagen, Laurent Petit, Emanuele Olivetti, Jonathan Masci, Davide Boscaini and Paolo Avesani
arxiv-2003-11013.description: Abstract Tractograms are virtual representations of the white matter fibers of the brain. They are of primary interest for tasks like presurgical planning, and investigation of neuroplasticity or brain disorders. Each tractogram is composed of millions of fibers encoded as 3D polylines.

arxiv-2010-13015.title: Towards Interaction Detection Using Topological Analysis on Neural Networks
arxiv-2010-13015.creator: Zirui Liu, Qingquan Song, Kaixiong Zhou, Ting-Hsiang Wang, Ying Shan, Xia Hu
arxiv-2010-13015.description: Abstract Detecting statistical interactions between input features is a crucial and challenging task. Recent advances demonstrate that it is possible to extract learned interactions from trained neural networks. It has also been observed that, in neural networks, any interacting features must follow a strongly weighted connection to common hidden units.

arxiv-2102-05144.title: Toward Safe and Efficient Human–Robot Interaction via Behavior-Driven Danger Signaling
arxiv-2102-05144.creator: Mehdi Hosseinzadeh, Bruno Sinopoli, Aaron F. Bobick
arxiv-2102-05144.description: Abstract This paper introduces the notion of danger awareness in the context of Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), which decodes whether a human is aware of the existence of the robot, and illuminates whether the human is willing to engage in enforcing the safety.

arxiv-2310-05907.title: Stochastic wave equation with heavy-tailed noise: Uniqueness of solutions and past light-cone property
arxiv-2310-05907.creator: Juan J. Jiménez
arxiv-2310-05907.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Juan J. Jiménez. In this article, we study the stochastic wave equation in spatial dimensions d ≤ 2 d\leq 2 with multiplicative Lévy noise that can have infinite p p -th moments. Using the past light-cone property of the wave equation, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a solution, considering only the p p -integrability of the Lévy measure ν \nu for the region corresponding to the small jumps of the noise.

arxiv-2404-04243.title: Identity Decoupling for Multi-Subject Personalization of Text-to-Image Models
arxiv-2404-04243.creator: Sangwon Jang, Jaehyeong Jo, Kimin Lee, Sung Ju Hwang ∗ Equal contribution † Equal advising, KAIST, DeepAuto.ai { sangwon.jang, harryjo97, kiminlee, sjhwang82 }@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2404-04243.description: Abstract Text-to-image diffusion models have shown remarkable success in generating personalized subjects based on a few reference images. However, current methods often fail when generating multiple subjects simultaneously, resulting in mixed identities with combined attributes from different subjects. In this work, we present MuDI, a novel framework that enables multi-subject personalization by effectively decoupling identities from multiple subjects.

arxiv-2409-19161.title: Toda field theories and Calogero models associated to infinite Weyl groups
arxiv-2409-19161.creator: Andreas Fring
arxiv-2409-19161.description: Abstract Many integrable theories can be formulated universally in terms of Lie algebraic root systems. Well-studied are conformally invariant scalar field theories of Toda type and their massive versions, which can be expressed in terms of simple roots of finite Lie and affine Kac-Moody algebras, respectively.

arxiv-2410-12867.title: Empowering Dysarthric Speech: Leveraging Advanced LLMs for Accurate Speech Correction and Multimodal Emotion Analysis
arxiv-2410-12867.creator: Kaushal Attaluri, Anirudh Chebolu, Sireesha Chittepu
arxiv-2410-12867.description: Abstract Dysarthria or Dysarthric speech as called is kind of a motor speech disorder which is caused by neurological damage that affects the muscles for speech production, which results in slurred, slow, or difficult-to-understand speech which has been affecting millions of people worldwide including those with conditions such as stroke, traumatic brain injury, cerebral palsy, Parkinson’s disease, and multiple sclerosis,

arxiv-2411-03110.title: Multiple-basis representation of quantum states
arxiv-2411-03110.creator: Adrián Pérez-Salinas, Patrick Emonts, Jordi Tura, Vedran Dunjko
arxiv-2411-03110.description: Abstract Classical simulation of quantum physics is a central approach to investigating physical phenomena. Quantum computers enhance computational capabilities beyond those of classical resources, but it remains unclear to what extent existing limited quantum computers can contribute to this enhancement. In this work, we explore a new hybrid, efficient quantum-classical representation of quantum states, the multiple-basis representation.

arxiv-2501-13063.title: Sharp regularity estimates for quasi-linear elliptic dead core problems and applications
arxiv-2501-13063.creator: João Vítor da Silva and Ariel M. Salort
arxiv-2501-13063.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by João Vítor da Silva and Ariel M. Salort. In this manuscript we study geometric regularity estimates for quasi-linear elliptic equations of p p -Laplace type ( 1 < p < ∞ 1<p<\infty ) with strong absorption condition: − div ⁡ ( Φ ⁡ ( x , u , ∇ u ) ) + λ 0 ​ ( x ) ​ u + q ​ ( x ) = 0 in Ω ⊂ ℝ N , -\mathrm{div}(\Phi(x,u,\nabla u))+\lambda_{0}(x)u_{+}^{q}(x)=0\quad\mbox{in}\quad\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{N}, where Φ : Ω × ℝ +

arxiv-2502-13257.title: Random Forest Autoencoders for Guided Representation Learning
arxiv-2502-13257.creator: Adrien Aumon, Shuang Ni, Myriam Lizotte, Guy Wolf, Kevin R. Moon, Jake S. Rhodes
arxiv-2502-13257.description: Abstract Extensive research has produced robust methods for unsupervised data visualization. Yet supervised visualization—where expert labels guide representations—remains underexplored, as most supervised approaches prioritize classification over visualization. Recently, RF-PHATE, a diffusion-based manifold learning method leveraging random forests and information geometry, marked significant progress in supervised visualization.

arxiv-2505-03761.title: Soft yet Effective Robots via Holistic Co-Design
arxiv-2505-03761.creator: Maximilian Stölzle, Niccolò Pagliarani, Francesco Stella, Josie Hughes, Cecilia Laschi, Daniela Rus, Matteo Cianchetti, Cosimo Della Santina, Gioele Zardini
arxiv-2505-03761.description: Abstract Soft robots promise inherent safety via their material compliance for seamless interactions with humans or delicate environments. Despite progress, the field struggles to balance task-specific performance with broader factors like durability and manufacturability—a difficulty that we find is compounded by traditional sequential design processes with their lack of feedback loops.

arxiv-2507-04960.title: Distributed Approximation Algorithms for Minimum Dominating Set in Locally Nice Graphs
arxiv-2507-04960.creator: Marthe Bonamy, Cyril Gavoille, Timothé Picavet, Alexandra Wesolek
arxiv-2507-04960.description: Abstract We give a new, short proof that graphs embeddable in a given Euler genus- g g surface admit a simple f ⁡ ( g ) f(g) -round α \alpha -approximation distributed algorithm for Minimum Dominating Set (MDS), where the approximation ratio α ⩽ 906 \alpha\leqslant 906 . Using tricks from Heydt et al.

arxiv-2508-05546.title: Modular Architecture for High-Performance and Low Overhead Data Transfers
arxiv-2508-05546.creator: Rasman Mubtasim Swargo, Engin Arslan, Md Arifuzzaman
arxiv-2508-05546.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rasman Mubtasim Swargo, Engin Arslan, Md Arifuzzaman. High-performance applications necessitate rapid and dependable transfer of massive datasets across geographically dispersed locations. Traditional file transfer tools often suffer from resource underutilization and instability due to fixed configurations or monolithic optimization methods. We propose AutoMDT , a novel Modular Data Transfer Architecture, to address these issues by employing deep reinforcement learning based agent to simultaneously optimize concurrency levels for read, network, and write operations.

arxiv-2508-11305.title: Defects4Log: Benchmarking LLMs for Logging Code Defect Detection and Reasoning *Corresponding authors.
arxiv-2508-11305.creator: Xin Wang, Zhenhao Li *, Zishuo Ding *
arxiv-2508-11305.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xin Wang, Zhenhao Li *, Zishuo Ding *. Logging code is written by developers to capture system runtime behavior and plays a vital role in debugging, performance analysis, and system monitoring. However, defects in logging code can undermine the usefulness of logs and lead to misinterpretations.

arxiv-2510-18576.title: Large values of derivatives of the Riemann zeta function on vertical homogeneous progressions
arxiv-2510-18576.creator: Qiyu Yang 1, Shengbo Zhao 2
arxiv-2510-18576.description: Abstract . In this paper, we establish lower bounds for the maximum of derivatives of the Riemann zeta function on vertical homogeneous progressions. When the real part σ \sigma lies within a suitable range, we show that the discrete case has a similar order of magnitude to the continuous case, using the resonance method.

plos-pone-0012222.title: Hybrid Models Identified a 12-Gene Signature for Lung Cancer Prognosis and Chemoresponse Prediction
plos-pone-0012222.creator: Ying-Wooi Wan, Ebrahim Sabbagh, Rebecca Raese et al.
plos-pone-0012222.description: PLOS ONE research article. Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. The recurrence rate ranges from 35–50% among early stage non-small cell lung cancer patients. To date, there is no fully-validated and clinically applied prognostic gene signature for personalized treatment

pmc-10628809.title: Protocol for screening cellular outputs activated by optogenetically controlled temporal PI3K signaling activation patterns
pmc-10628809.creator: Yoshibumi Ueda, Shohei Matsushita, Mitsugu Suzuki, Takeaki Ozawa
pmc-10628809.description: SummaryPI3K signaling elicits distinct outputs in response to different patterns of extracellular stimulation. Here, we present a protocol for screening cellular outputs activated by optogenetically controlled temporal PI3K signaling activation patterns in 96-well plates. We describe steps for establishing PPAP2-stable cells, probe expression, and blue light irradiation. We then detail procedures for analysis of translation activity.

pmc-11436104.title: Cyanobacterial Cyclic Peptides Can Disrupt Cytoskeleton Organization in Human Astrocytes—A Contribution to the Understanding of the Systemic Toxicity of Cyanotoxins
pmc-11436104.creator: Anja Bubik, Robert Frangež, Monika C. Žužek, Ion Gutiérrez-Aguirre, Tamara T. Lah, Bojan Sedmak
pmc-11436104.description: The systemic toxicity of cyclic peptides produced by cyanobacteria (CCPs) is not yet completely understood. Apart from the most known damages to the liver and kidneys, symptoms of their neurotoxicity have also been reported. Hepatotoxic CCPs, like microcystins, as well as non-hepatotoxic anabaenopeptins and planktopeptins, all exhibit cytotoxic and cytostatic effects on mammalian cells.

pmc-12052426.title: A scoping review of transmission models for soil-transmitted helminth infections to underpin the development of a transmission model for Strongyloides stercoralis
pmc-12052426.creator: Mackrina Winslow, Juan Pablo Villanueva-Cabezas, Vito Colella, Patricia T. Campbell
pmc-12052426.description: t Asia (Brooker et al., 2006; Pullan et al., 2014). The term STH encompasses a group of parasitic nematodes, including roundworm (Ascaris lumbricoides), whipworm (Trichuris trichiura), hookworms (Necator americanus, Ancylostoma ceylanicum and Ancylostoma duodenale) and Strongyloides stercoralis (Colella et al., 2021; World Health Organization, 2023).

pmc-12531484.title: Spatially resolved transcriptomics reveals a unique disease signature and potential biomarkers for chronic traumatic encephalopathy
pmc-12531484.creator: Catherine M Suter, Jennifer E Cropley, Andrew J Affleck, Maggie Lee, Karina Hammond, Brian Gloss, Michael E Buckland
pmc-12531484.description: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a poorly understood environmental tauopathy uniquely associated with repetitive head injury. It is clinically ambiguous and at present can only be diagnosed post-mortem. There is a pressing need to understand CTE pathophysiology in order to identify targets for possible intervention and biomarkers for in-life diagnosis.

pmc-13165484.title: On Exposure Definition and Temporal Interpretation in the Reported Association Between Number of Pregnancies and Rheumatoid Arthritis [Response to Letter]
pmc-13165484.creator: Wenjie Sheng, Zhengguang Hu, Zhaokai Ma, Qinwen Feng, Nianmei Chen
pmc-13165484.description: In NHANES, this variable is based on the self-reported question, “How many times have you been pregnant?” It therefore reflects lifetime pregnancy count, but does not distinguish live birth, miscarriage, induced abortion, or other pregnancy outcomes. This is an important point, and we agree that these reproductive factors should not be treated as interchangeable.

pmc-13220550.title: Facilitators, barriers, and factors determining the willingness to donate human milk among postpartum mothers in a tertiary women’s hospital in Nepal: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13220550.creator: Chandra Singh Sejuwal, Bishow Kandel, Samikshya Badal, Dinesh Raj Neupane, Sunny Kumar Yadav, Rojina Basnet, Khem Bahadur Karki
pmc-13220550.description: BackgroundBreastfeeding is universally acknowledged as the most effective and efficient means of ensuring optimal growth, development, and survival of infants. However, in rare cases where breastfeeding is medically contraindicated or the mother’s milk is insufficient, donor human milk from a milk bank serves as a critical alternative.

pmc-13452078.title: Association Between Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease and Subclinical Atherosclerosis Assessed by Carotid Intima-Media Thickness: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13452078.creator: Nasrin Akter, Mst Fatema Firoz, Farzana Akter Shifa, Kabbya Kumar Datta, Tasnuva Islam, Md Zahidul Alam Khan Sykot, Md Akib Akram, Md Khaledur Rahman, Md Atik Shahryar
pmc-13452078.description: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is variably associated with subclinical atherosclerosis, measured using carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), although findings across studies remain inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between NAFLD and subclinical atherosclerosis, assessed by CIMT, and to explore possible sources of heterogeneity.

pmc-13464310.title: Ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells from human mobilized peripheral blood for gene therapy applications
pmc-13464310.creator: Erika Zonari, Matteo Maria Naldini, Matteo Barcella, Monica Volpin, Francesca Vincenti, Giacomo Desantis, Leila Hadadi, Carolina Caserta, Ilaria Galasso, Beatrice Martini, Federico Midena, Giacomo Farina, Roberta Vacca, Francesca Tucci, Leonardo Ormoli, Ilaria Visigalli, Michela Vezzoli, Dejan Lazar
pmc-13464310.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ex vivo expansion of mobilized peripheral blood (mPB) hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) represents a promising approach to advance cell and gene therapy strategies yet is hampered by loss of stem cell function when applying commonly used culture protocols. We performed in-depth characterization of mPB expansion cultures by single-cell RNA sequencing, which highlighted differentiation trajectories with preservation of lineage fidelity in committed progenitors.

uslaw-usc-t18-s3624.title: 18 U.S.C. § 3624 — Release of a prisoner
uslaw-usc-t18-s3624.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s3624.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part II (Criminal Procedure); Chapter 229 (Postsentence Administration); Subchapter C (Imprisonment). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Date of Release.— A prisoner shall be released by the Bureau of Prisons on the date of the expiration of the prisoner’s term of imprisonment, less any time credited toward the service of the prisoner’s sentence.
